options: Treat as potentially full stomach and consider gastric POCUS or delay
Proceed routinely because fasting time is adequate
Give prophylaxis and proceed without further assessment
Encourage clear liquids immediately before surgery
questions.explanation: GLP-1 agonists delay gastric emptying; POCUS or longer fasting may be needed.

questions.stem: A patient drank a latte containing milk 3 hours before elective anesthesia, while another drank plain black coffee at the same time. Why can their fasting status differ?
options: Milk makes the latte a non-clear liquid requiring a longer interval
All coffee beverages qualify as clear liquids
Both are acceptable after 2 hours regardless of additives
Black coffee requires a longer interval than milk-containing coffee
questions.explanation: Non-human milk requires 6 hours; a latte is not a clear liquid.

questions.stem: A cirrhotic patient has bilirubin 4, albumin 2.4, INR 2.1, ascites, and mild encephalopathy. Which Child-Pugh class is most likely?
questions.explanation: These values indicate decompensated disease, consistent with Child-Pugh C.

questions.stem: A cirrhotic patient has MELD 18 and requests elective hernia repair. Which next step best follows the lecture threshold?
questions.explanation: MELD >15 typically prompts transplant evaluation before elective non-hepatic surgery.

questions.stem: A dialysis patient last dialyzed 2 days ago and now has potassium 5.9 mEq/L before elective surgery. Which issue should be corrected first?
options: Hyperkalemia, potentially with dialysis or other therapy
questions.explanation: Hyperkalemia requires correction before surgery; timing of last dialysis matters.

questions.stem: Which postoperative analgesic strategy is safest for a dialysis patient after fistula revision?
options: Avoid morphine, meperidine, and NSAIDs when possible
Use morphine PCA with a basal infusion
Use meperidine for pain and shivering
questions.explanation: Morphine and meperidine have active metabolites that accumulate in renal failure, and NSAIDs threaten residual renal function.

questions.stem: A patient has a functioning AV fistula in the left arm. Where should the BP cuff and IV be placed?
options: On the right arm, avoiding the fistula extremity
On the left arm near the fistula
On the left arm distal to the fistula
Either arm if monitoring is brief
questions.explanation: Protect the fistula arm from cuffs, IVs, and blood draws.

questions.stem: A patient reports prior anaphylaxis to rocuronium. What is the most appropriate implication for the anesthetic plan?
options: Avoid rocuronium and choose an alternative neuromuscular blocker strategy
Use rocuronium only for short cases
Assume the event was a minor side effect
questions.explanation: NMBs are common allergy triggers; true anaphylaxis requires avoidance and planning.

questions.stem: A patient reports gastrointestinal upset after ciprofloxacin without rash, swelling, bronchospasm, or hypotension. How should this be classified?
options: Adverse drug reaction rather than true allergy
A reaction requiring avoidance of all quinolones
questions.explanation: GI upset with antibiotics is a common adverse drug reaction.

questions.stem: A chronic heavy drinker last drank 6 hours ago and is already tremulous and tachycardic. Which priority comes before elective anesthesia?
options: Proceed and treat only after induction
Delay six months before any surgery
questions.explanation: Alcohol withdrawal can be managed with benzodiazepines or dexmedetomidine/clonidine.

questions.stem: A patient with recent cocaine use has severe hypertension and tachycardia. Which medication should generally be avoided because of unopposed alpha stimulation?
questions.explanation: Beta-blockers can cause unopposed alpha stimulation in cocaine intoxication.

questions.stem: A patient maintained on buprenorphine needs painful knee surgery. Which perioperative analgesic strategy is most appropriate?
options: Multimodal analgesia with regional techniques when appropriate
Stop buprenorphine and avoid all opioids
questions.explanation: OUD patients may need higher opioid doses and benefit from multimodal and regional techniques.

questions.stem: A patient has BMI 42, OSA requiring CPAP, and hypertension. Which ASA class best reflects the overall systemic disease burden under the cited criterion?
questions.explanation: BMI ≥40 places a patient in ASA III.

questions.stem: A 58-year-old man has BMI 36, snoring, hypertension, and neck circumference 43 cm. What is his STOP-BANG score?
questions.explanation: Snoring, pressure, BMI >35, age >50, neck >40, male = 6.

questions.stem: A 45-year-old woman is a nonsmoker with prior PONV, and the plan avoids postoperative opioids. Which Apfel score should guide prophylaxis?
questions.explanation: Female, PONV hx, nonsmoker = 3.

questions.stem: An older patient with dementia and poor vision is scheduled for hip surgery. Which neurologic complication deserves particular attention during perioperative planning?
questions.explanation: Advanced age, cognitive impairment, and sensory deficits are delirium risk factors.

questions.stem: A pacemaker patient with complete heart block is scheduled for a case using monopolar cautery. Which preoperative question most directly determines the consequence of pacing inhibition?
options: When was the battery last replaced?
questions.explanation: Pacemaker dependence determines risk if EMI inhibits pacing.

questions.stem: An ICD patient reports two shocks in the past month. What should that history trigger before surgery?
options: Evaluation of recent arrhythmias and device function
No interrogation if the patient feels well
questions.explanation: Recent shocks suggest active arrhythmias; interrogation and cardiology input are needed.

questions.stem: A patient has EF 30% and dyspnea at rest before elective knee replacement. Which finding should drive management?
options: Decompensated heart failure requires optimization before elective surgery
Spinal anesthesia makes immediate surgery acceptable
Invasive monitoring alone offsets the risk
Normal blood pressure would permit proceeding
questions.explanation: Decompensated HF is a red flag requiring evaluation before elective surgery.

questions.stem: A patient with remote MI and stable CAD walks 3 miles daily without symptoms. What does the functional history suggest?
options: Adequate reserve with no routine need for further cardiac testing in the absence of active disease
questions.explanation: Good functional capacity without active symptoms usually means no further testing.

questions.stem: A diabetic patient has glucose 240 mg/dL before scheduled surgery. Which approach best follows the lecture threshold?
options: Treat the hyperglycemia and reassess whether proceeding is appropriate
questions.explanation: Treat glucose above 180; delay is considered when it exceeds 300.

questions.stem: A chronic steroid user is scheduled for colonoscopy. Which regimen best matches the table's minor-procedure recommendation?
options: Usual dose plus hydrocortisone 50 mg IV, then 25 mg every 8 hours
Hydrocortisone 100 mg IV plus 200 mg over 24 hours
questions.explanation: Colonoscopy is listed as minor; the plan is usual dose plus 50 mg IV and 25 mg q8h for 24 h.

questions.stem: A chronic steroid user is scheduled for dental extraction. Which regimen best matches the lowest-stress category in the table?
options: Hydrocortisone 50 mg IV then 25 mg every 8 hours
questions.explanation: Superficial procedures like dental extraction need only the usual daily dose.

questions.stem: A healthy woman of childbearing potential is scheduled for diagnostic laparoscopy. Which routine preoperative test is specifically indicated?
questions.explanation: Labs are history based; a healthy woman of childbearing age needs pregnancy testing.

questions.stem: A patient undergoing a Whipple is expected to have substantial blood loss. Which preoperative laboratory value most directly informs anemia and transfusion planning?
questions.explanation: H&H is indicated when significant blood loss is expected.

questions.stem: A patient has documented prior difficult intubation and now requires general anesthesia. Which preparation best reduces the chance that the same problem becomes a crisis?
options: Have videolaryngoscopy, positioning aids, and a difficult-airway cart immediately available
Use only the standard intubation setup
Choose MAC solely to avoid airway management
Perform awake intubation in every patient with any prior difficulty
questions.explanation: Anticipating difficult airway means preparing VL, positioning aids, and the difficult airway cart.

questions.stem: A patient had a drug-eluting stent 5 months ago and now takes aspirin alone. Which plan best follows the lecture timing and antiplatelet principles?
options: Proceed with elective surgery and continue aspirin
questions.explanation: DES timing is 3–6 months with aspirin continued.

questions.stem: A patient has a holosystolic murmur loudest at the apex that radiates toward the axilla. Which valve lesion best explains the finding?
questions.explanation: MR is holosystolic at the apex radiating to the axilla.

questions.stem: Two heart-failure patients face the same operation; one has EF 55% and the other EF 30%. Which statement is most accurate?
options: The patient with preserved EF generally has lower perioperative risk than the patient with HFrEF
The patient with preserved EF has higher perioperative risk
questions.explanation: HFpEF (EF above 50%) carries lower perioperative risk than HFrEF.

questions.stem: An asthmatic patient has frequent rescue-inhaler use and required oral steroids last month. Which issue matters most before elective anesthesia?
options: Poor asthma control with possible HPA-axis suppression
Higher MAC from chronic steroid exposure
questions.explanation: Recent steroids and frequent rescue use suggest poor control and potential adrenal suppression.

questions.stem: A smoker quit 3 days before surgery and asks whether stopping this late still helped. Which response is most accurate?
options: Yes; even brief abstinence lowers carboxyhemoglobin and may provide benefit
No benefit occurs until after 2 months
Smoking status has little anesthetic relevance
questions.explanation: Even a few days of cessation lowers carboxyhemoglobin and improves oxygen delivery.

questions.stem: A chronic heavy drinker is sober today. A colleague expects a lower MAC because acute alcohol lowers anesthetic requirement. What is the better interpretation?
options: Chronic tolerance tends to increase MAC when the patient is not acutely intoxicated
Chronic use lowers MAC for the same reason as acute intoxication
Acute and chronic alcohol have no meaningful effect on MAC
questions.explanation: Acute intoxication decreases MAC, whereas chronic alcohol exposure produces tolerance and tends to increase MAC when the patient is sober.

questions.stem: An acutely alcohol-intoxicated patient requires emergency surgery. Compared with the same patient when sober, what change in volatile anesthetic requirement should be anticipated?
options: Higher MAC from acute enzyme induction
questions.explanation: Acute alcohol decreases MAC.

questions.stem: A patient with chronic methamphetamine use has severe dental decay and HR 120. Which paired anesthetic concerns are most relevant?
options: Reduced airway risk and lower anesthetic requirement
questions.explanation: Methamphetamine causes poor dentition and SNS activation.

questions.stem: A patient with severe GERD is at elevated aspiration risk. Which prophylactic combination best reduces gastric acidity with a nonparticulate antacid?
options: An H2 blocker plus sodium citrate
questions.explanation: GERD is an aspiration risk; Pepcid and Bicitra reduce acid and particulate risk.

questions.stem: A child received infant formula 5 hours before anesthesia. Which fasting interpretation is correct?
options: The interval is insufficient because formula requires 6 hours
The interval is adequate because formula requires 4 hours
The interval is adequate because formula requires 2 hours
questions.explanation: Infant formula requires 6 hours.

questions.stem: An infant had breast milk 4.5 hours before anesthesia. Which fasting interpretation is correct?
options: The interval is adequate because breast milk requires 4 hours
The interval is insufficient because breast milk requires 6 hours
The interval is insufficient because breast milk requires 8 hours
questions.explanation: Breast milk requires 4 hours.

questions.stem: A patient has RCRI 1, functional capacity at least 4 METs, and no active cardiac condition. Which next step is most appropriate?
options: Proceed without routine additional cardiac testing
Repeat stress testing before any elective surgery
questions.explanation: Low RCRI and good functional capacity usually mean no further testing.

questions.stem: A patient has RCRI 3, functional capacity below 4 METs, and is scheduled for major vascular surgery. Which feature combination most strongly supports additional cardiac risk assessment?
options: High clinical risk plus poor functional capacity before a high-risk operation
questions.explanation: High RCRI and poor capacity prompt further evaluation.

questions.stem: A patient benefits hemodynamically from maintaining coordinated atrial contraction followed by ventricular contraction. Which feature of DDD pacing is most relevant?
questions.explanation: DDD maintains AV synchrony.

questions.stem: Why might a pacemaker be placed temporarily in VOO during surgery with significant EMI exposure?
options: Asynchronous output prevents cautery from inhibiting ventricular pacing
It increases heart rate with activity
questions.explanation: VOO is asynchronous and used when EMI is expected.

questions.stem: A patient has a new irregular rhythm accompanied by dizziness before elective surgery. Which finding makes this different from stable rate-controlled atrial fibrillation?
options: The arrhythmia is new and symptomatic, so it requires evaluation first
Starting a beta-blocker automatically makes surgery safe
Symptoms do not affect perioperative significance
questions.explanation: New-onset arrhythmias with symptoms require cardiac workup.

questions.stem: A patient presents for elective surgery with BP 185/115 mmHg and headache. Which feature should drive postponement and further evaluation?
options: Severe hypertension with possible end-organ symptoms
The pressure is acceptable because it is below 200/120
A beta-blocker bolus is sufficient preparation
Hypertension is too common to affect elective planning
questions.explanation: BP above 180/110 with symptoms suggests end-organ risk; elective surgery should be delayed.

questions.stem: A patient has remote myocardial infarction but no active symptoms. Which ASA class best reflects established significant systemic disease?
questions.explanation: A remote MI (more than 3 months ago) is an ASA III example; a recent MI is ASA IV.

questions.stem: A patient with severe COPD is usually ASA III, but he now has unstable angina before urgent surgery. Which finding is what elevates the classification to ASA IV?
options: Unstable angina creating a constant threat to life
The urgent timing of surgery alone
questions.explanation: ASA IV reflects severe systemic disease that is a constant threat to life. In this scenario, unstable angina is the feature that pushes the classification beyond ASA III.

questions.stem: A patient using an insulin pump is scheduled for a 5-hour prone spine procedure. Which factors most directly determine whether pump therapy can be continued safely?
options: The pump eliminates the need for glucose monitoring
questions.explanation: Pump considerations include procedure length, positioning, and radiation or cautery.

questions.stem: A patient reports taking St. John's wort daily but did not list it under medications. Why is identifying this supplement relevant before anesthesia?
options: It can interact with anesthetic and perioperative medications
Abrupt discontinuation predictably causes life-threatening withdrawal
Reducing it to half-dose eliminates all perioperative interactions
Herbal supplements have no clinically relevant anesthetic effects
questions.explanation: Herbal supplements are held. St. John's wort induces CYP enzymes and alters anesthetic drug metabolism.

questions.stem: A patient with epilepsy takes levetiracetam. Which morning-of-surgery plan best minimizes perioperative seizure risk?
questions.explanation: Antiseizure medications are taken.

questions.stem: A patient with Parkinson disease skipped levodopa on the morning of surgery. Which consequence is most relevant?
options: Worsening rigidity and dysphagia may increase aspiration and mobility problems
questions.explanation: Parkinson's meds are taken to avoid rigidity and aspiration risk.

questions.stem: A patient has a family history suggestive of malignant hyperthermia. Which preoperative plan is most appropriate?
options: Ignore the history if the patient has had prior surgery
questions.explanation: MH or family MH history should lead to a non-triggering plan.

questions.stem: A patient reports becoming acutely confused, combative, and disoriented while waking from a previous anesthetic, without nausea or allergic symptoms. Which prior anesthetic complication should be documented?
questions.explanation: Emergence delirium is part of anesthesia history.

questions.stem: A patient has both prior PONV and motion sickness. Which implication is most appropriate?
options: PONV risk is increased and prophylaxis should be planned
Risk increases only if postoperative opioids are used
questions.explanation: PONV history is an Apfel factor; motion sickness also suggests higher risk.

questions.stem: A dialysis patient's usual BP is 160/95, then falls to 90/50 after induction. Why can that pressure be dangerous even though hypotension is common after induction?
options: The large relative decrease may compromise organ perfusion
It is an ideal target for dialysis patients
questions.explanation: The notes caution not to let BP get too low in patients with high baseline BP.

questions.stem: Using the lecture's ideal-body-weight formula, a 5-foot-8-inch man has IBW about 68.4 kg and actual weight 120 kg. Approximately how many times IBW is his actual weight?
A 5-foot-2-inch woman with obesity needs a medication dosed using ideal body weight. Using the lecture formula, which approximate IBW is correct?
A patient weighs 110 kg at 1.65 m and is being screened for obesity-related anesthetic risk. Which BMI category applies?
questions.explanation: 110 ÷ 2.72 ≈ 40.4, which is class III (≥40).

questions.stem: A patient weighs 95 kg at 1.75 m. Which BMI class applies?
questions.explanation: 95 ÷ 3.06 ≈ 31.0, which is class I.

questions.stem: A patient has BMI 41, OSA requiring CPAP, and controlled hypertension. Which summary best integrates ASA status and airway/respiratory risk?
options: ASA III with elevated OSA and difficult-airway concerns
ASA II with low OSA risk and routine airway
ASA III with low OSA risk and routine airway
questions.explanation: BMI ≥40 = ASA III, and obesity with OSA raises airway and cardiopulmonary risk.

questions.stem: A woman snores, has daytime fatigue and witnessed apnea, BMI 38, neck 38 cm, no hypertension, and age under 50. What STOP-BANG category results?
questions.explanation: S, T, O, B = 4. Age <50, female, neck ≤40 cm. 3–4 is intermediate.

questions.stem: A 70-year-old man snores, has hypertension, BMI 36, neck 42 cm, and witnessed apnea. What STOP-BANG category results?
questions.explanation: S, O, P, B, A, N, G = 7 (no tiredness). 5–8 is high.

questions.stem: A patient has RCRI 2, functional capacity at least 4 METs, and no active cardiac symptoms before laparoscopic colectomy. Which estimate and plan best fit?
options: About 2.4% MACE risk; proceed without routine additional testing
questions.explanation: RCRI 2 = 2.4%. With ≥4 METs and no active disease, testing is usually not needed.

questions.stem: A patient uses insulin, has prior TIA, creatinine 1.6 mg/dL, and is scheduled for total knee arthroplasty. What is the RCRI score?
questions.explanation: Insulin DM (1) and cerebrovascular disease (1) = 2. Cr 1.6 does not count; knee is not high-risk surgery.

questions.stem: A patient had a bare-metal stent 20 days ago and now requests elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy. Which timing issue controls the decision?
options: The case should wait until more than 30 days after BMS placement
Aspirin continuation makes immediate surgery acceptable
Stopping aspirin makes immediate surgery acceptable
questions.explanation: BMS requires >30 days before elective surgery.

questions.stem: A patient is 4 months after CABG, has excellent functional capacity, and wants elective shoulder surgery. How should the reassuring functional status affect the lecture's CABG timing recommendation?
options: It should not override the recommendation to wait more than 6 months after CABG
It permits immediate surgery because functional capacity is adequate
It reduces the waiting interval to 60 days
It eliminates the timing concern if regional anesthesia is used
questions.explanation: Good functional capacity does not replace the lecture's timing recommendation to wait more than 6 months after CABG for elective surgery.

questions.stem: An asymptomatic patient has an aortic valve area of 1.7 cm² and mean gradient 18 mmHg. Which severity category best matches both measurements?
questions.explanation: Mild AS: gradient <20 mmHg and area >1.5 cm².

questions.stem: A patient with prior rheumatic fever has exertional dyspnea and a low-pitched diastolic apical rumble preceded by an opening snap. Which lesion is most likely?
questions.explanation: A diastolic rumble with an opening snap after rheumatic fever is mitral stenosis, part of the diastolic MSARD group.

questions.stem: A patient had a medically managed MI 45 days ago and requests elective hip replacement. Which timing recommendation is most appropriate?
options: Delay until at least 60 days after the MI
Proceed because more than 30 days have passed
questions.explanation: MI without intervention requires 60 days before elective surgery.

questions.stem: A fasting patient with type 2 diabetes normally takes metformin and glipizide in the morning. Which instruction best limits medication-related hypoglycemia on the day of surgery?
questions.explanation: Hold oral diabetic medications on the morning of surgery.

questions.stem: A patient with type 1 diabetes uses basal glargine and will be fasting for surgery. Which insulin strategy best balances hypoglycemia against complete insulin omission?
options: Give about half the usual basal dose
Give the full dose specifically to prevent ketosis
questions.explanation: Insulin is typically reduced by about half on the day of surgery; type 1 diabetics need some basal insulin.

questions.stem: A chronic prednisone user is scheduled for laparoscopic cholecystectomy. Which regimen best matches the table's moderate-stress coverage?
options: Usual dose plus hydrocortisone 50 mg IV, then 25 mg every 8 hours
Hydrocortisone 100 mg IV then 200 mg over 24 hours
questions.explanation: Lap chole is similar to minor to moderate stress; the table gives usual dose plus 50 mg IV then 25 mg q8h.

questions.stem: A chronic steroid user is scheduled for major cardiac surgery. Which regimen best matches the table's major-stress recommendation?
options: Hydrocortisone 100 mg IV followed by 200 mg over 24 hours
Hydrocortisone 50 mg IV then 25 mg every 8 hours
questions.explanation: Major surgery requires 100 mg IV and 200 mg over 24 h, then taper.

questions.stem: A patient with Addison disease develops persistent hypotension that does not respond adequately to phenylephrine. Which treatment addresses the underlying problem?
questions.explanation: Adrenal insufficiency causes refractory hypotension; treat with corticosteroids.

questions.stem: A cirrhotic patient has normal aminotransferases but INR 1.8 and albumin 2.6 g/dL. Which hepatic function is most clearly impaired despite the absence of marked injury markers?
questions.explanation: INR and albumin reflect synthetic liver function.

questions.stem: A cirrhotic patient has platelets 60,000/µL without acute bleeding. Which mechanism is most likely?
questions.explanation: Thrombocytopenia in cirrhosis is largely from splenomegaly and sequestration.

questions.stem: A dialysis patient completed dialysis this morning. Which laboratory set is most important before proceeding because dialysis can rapidly change electrolytes and renal indices?
questions.explanation: The notes want a current renal panel, especially if recently dialyzed.

questions.stem: A dialysis patient has a functioning AV fistula in one arm and needs an arterial line. Which site best protects future dialysis access?
questions.explanation: Protect the fistula arm from lines and cuffs.

questions.stem: A patient had anaphylaxis to cefazolin and needs perioperative antibiotic prophylaxis. Which alternative from the lecture is most appropriate?
questions.explanation: Clindamycin is listed as an alternative.

questions.stem: During an antibiotic infusion, a patient develops flushing and hypotension without the broader pattern of IgE-mediated anaphylaxis. Which medication is classically associated with histamine-mediated infusion reactions?
questions.explanation: Vancomycin is listed as a histamine releaser.

questions.stem: A long-term smoker has chronic morning cough and sputum production. Which anesthetic implication follows most directly?
options: Possible COPD with increased secretions and reactive-airway risk
Lower bronchospasm risk from chronic airway exposure
questions.explanation: Heavy long-term smokers often have COPD with more secretions and airway reactivity.

questions.stem: A patient drinks 8 beers daily and is scheduled for major elective surgery. Which preoperative strategy best reduces alcohol-related complications when time allows?
options: Aim for at least 4 weeks of abstinence and plan for withdrawal risk
Stop only on the morning of surgery
questions.explanation: Abstinence for at least 4 weeks reduces complications; withdrawal risk must still be planned for.

questions.stem: A cocaine-intoxicated patient is hypertensive, tachycardic, and agitated. Which drug class should be used first to blunt the central sympathetic surge?
questions.explanation: Benzodiazepines are first-line for cocaine-induced sympathetic excess.

questions.stem: A patient maintained on naltrexone requires surgery. Which analgesic problem should be anticipated?
options: Opioid analgesia may be less effective because receptors are antagonized
questions.explanation: Opioid antagonists like naltrexone make mu-agonist pain control more difficult.

questions.stem: A patient has controlled hypertension and diabetes managed with metformin, with no functional limitation. Which ASA class best fits?
questions.explanation: Controlled HTN and DM without functional limitation are ASA II.

questions.stem: A patient has poorly controlled hypertension plus prior myocardial infarction but no current life-threatening instability. Which ASA class best fits?
questions.explanation: Poorly controlled HTN and prior MI are ASA III examples.

questions.stem: A patient with ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm requires immediate life-saving surgery and is unlikely to survive without it. Which classification applies?
questions.explanation: A ruptured AAA is an ASA V example; emergency adds E.

questions.stem: A patient has exactly one Apfel risk factor. What approximate baseline PONV probability should be used when deciding the intensity of prophylaxis?
questions.explanation: Score 1 corresponds to 20% risk.

questions.stem: A patient has none of the four Apfel risk factors. What approximate PONV probability remains even with a score of zero?
questions.explanation: Score 0 corresponds to 10% risk.

questions.stem: An airway exam shows Mallampati II but also a small mouth opening and beard. Which interpretation is most appropriate?
options: Multiple modest predictors can combine, so prepare for possible difficulty
Mallampati II overrides the other findings
A routine airway should be assumed
questions.explanation: Multiple minor abnormalities can create difficulty; plan accordingly.

questions.stem: Why is a detailed neurologic baseline especially important before carotid surgery?
options: It allows new postoperative neurologic deficits to be distinguished from preexisting findings
It determines whether regional anesthesia is permitted
questions.explanation: Carotid surgery is a listed indication for a detailed neuro exam.

questions.stem: A child has URI symptoms plus fever before elective surgery. Which feature should drive postponement?
options: Fever suggests more significant active infection
Children commonly have URIs, so proceed
Using an LMA removes the concern
questions.explanation: Proceeding is generally safe only if the child is not febrile or significantly symptomatic.

questions.stem: A COPD patient's stable baseline PaCO2 is 52 mmHg. How should that value be interpreted during perioperative planning?
options: Chronic compensated hypercapnia may be normal for this patient
questions.explanation: COPD patients may have baseline hypercarbia; interpret relative to baseline.

questions.stem: A patient with asthma stopped maintenance and rescue inhalers 2 days ago before surgery. What is the best instruction?
options: Resume prescribed inhalers through the perioperative period
Use albuterol only in preop and omit maintenance therapy
questions.explanation: The goal is to keep asthma meds up to surgery.

questions.stem: A patient with controlled hypothyroidism takes levothyroxine daily and is NPO for elective surgery. Which perioperative plan best preserves thyroid control?
options: Omit it solely because the patient is NPO
questions.explanation: Continue levothyroxine before surgery.

questions.stem: A diabetic patient has glucose 55 mg/dL in preop. Which problem takes priority before anesthesia?
options: Treat hypoglycemia with dextrose and reassess
Proceed after oral juice regardless of procedure timing
questions.explanation: Hypoglycemia should be treated; D10 or dextrose may be needed.

questions.stem: A patient on warfarin needs urgent surgery and has INR 2.8. Which principle best guides reversal?
options: Individualize reversal to bleeding risk, urgency, and thromboembolic risk
Give vitamin K and proceed immediately in every case
Stop warfarin and proceed without further consideration
Give vitamin K routinely to every warfarin patient
questions.explanation: Anticoagulant management is case by case; urgency, bleeding risk, and the indication guide reversal choices.

questions.stem: A patient with BMI 38 and STOP-BANG 6 is being considered for outpatient surgery. Which issue should most influence postoperative planning?
options: High OSA risk warrants careful monitoring and disposition decisions
No change is needed because the case is outpatient
OSA does not affect discharge planning
questions.explanation: High STOP-BANG and obesity increase risk; outpatient planning must be careful.

questions.stem: An ICD patient will undergo monopolar cautery. Which device-specific plan should be established before surgery?
options: How tachyarrhythmia therapies will be suspended and restored
Apply a magnet without knowing device response
Use bipolar cautery and skip device assessment
questions.explanation: ICD management requires knowing whether therapies can be suspended or a magnet is safe.

questions.stem: A patient with AAI pacing develops new complete AV block. Why is the existing mode now inadequate?
options: AAI depends on intact AV conduction to activate the ventricles
questions.explanation: AAI requires intact AV conduction; AV block makes it inadequate.

questions.stem: A pacemaker was last interrogated 3 years ago before elective surgery. What is the most appropriate next step?
options: Rely on the old interrogation if the patient feels well
questions.explanation: The last interrogation date is a key preop question.

questions.stem: A patient has never previously received anesthesia. Which uncertainty should remain part of the preoperative assessment?
options: Prior airway behavior and anesthetic drug reactions are unknown
Absence of prior complications proves low risk
A normal anesthetic response can be assumed
questions.explanation: Patients who have never had anesthesia need caution.

questions.stem: A healthy adult is scheduled for minor outpatient knee arthroscopy and has no routine laboratory studies. Which interpretation is most appropriate?
options: This can be appropriate because testing should be history- and procedure-driven
Every surgical patient needs CBC and BMP
Every surgical patient needs an ECG
Every surgical patient needs a chest radiograph
questions.explanation: Preop labs are history based; a healthy patient for a low-risk procedure may need none.

questions.stem: A procedure is expected to involve about 1,000 mL of blood loss. Which laboratory test most directly informs preoperative anemia and transfusion planning?
questions.explanation: H&H is indicated for significant blood loss.

questions.stem: A patient with BMI 29 kg/m² has no diagnosed comorbidities. Which weight category should be documented before evaluating additional risk factors?
questions.explanation: BMI 25–29.9 is overweight.

questions.stem: A patient with BMI 33 is being considered for outpatient surgery. What does the lecture suggest?
options: Screen carefully for obesity-related comorbidities and ambulatory suitability
Require inpatient admission solely because BMI exceeds 30
questions.explanation: BMI >30 should be carefully screened before outpatient placement.

questions.stem: A patient with stable CAD and remote MI is scheduled for cataract surgery. Which procedure-related cardiac risk category applies?
questions.explanation: Cataract surgery is low risk in the notes.

questions.stem: A patient with CAD is scheduled for major open abdominal surgery. How should the procedural cardiac stress be characterized relative to a superficial procedure?
questions.explanation: Abdominal procedures are intermediate risk, and intraperitoneal surgery counts as high-risk in RCRI.

questions.stem: A patient is 4 months after drug-eluting stent placement and takes aspirin. Which plan best follows the lecture's timing guidance?
options: Proceed if the 3–6 month interval is acceptable and continue aspirin
Delay every DES case until 12 months
questions.explanation: DES timing is 3–6 months with aspirin continued.

questions.stem: A patient has a documented latex allergy. Which intervention most directly prevents perioperative exposure?
options: Premedicate and otherwise use standard supplies
questions.explanation: The allergy slide asks about latex; latex-safe preparation is required.

questions.stem: A patient's family history is strongly suggestive of malignant hyperthermia. Which anesthetic preparation is most appropriate?
options: Give prophylactic dantrolene to every such patient
questions.explanation: Family MH history requires a trigger-free plan.

questions.stem: A patient with prior PONV is scheduled for laparoscopy. Which strategy best addresses the combined patient and procedural risk?
options: Prefer volatile anesthesia to reduce nausea
questions.explanation: PONV history increases Apfel score and supports prophylaxis.

questions.stem: A patient labels morphine as an allergy because it caused isolated itching without airway or hemodynamic symptoms. Which interpretation is most likely?
options: Histamine-mediated side effect rather than true IgE allergy
questions.explanation: Morphine is a histamine releaser; itching often reflects that effect.

questions.stem: Why is ideal body weight calculated in a patient with severe obesity?
options: Some anesthetic medications require a weight scalar other than total body weight
questions.explanation: IBW is used for medication dosing and is added to each care plan.

questions.stem: A patient with renal failure requests ketorolac. Which concern should guide the analgesic plan?
options: Avoid NSAIDs because they can worsen renal injury
questions.explanation: NSAIDs are restricted in renal failure.

questions.stem: OSA screening yields a STOP-BANG score of 2. Which risk category should guide perioperative interpretation?
questions.explanation: 0–2 is low risk.

questions.stem: OSA screening yields a STOP-BANG score of 5 before ambulatory surgery. Which risk category should influence monitoring and disposition planning?
questions.explanation: 5–8 is high risk.

questions.stem: A patient uses insulin, has CHF with EF 35%, creatinine 2.2 mg/dL, and is scheduled for total knee arthroplasty; she stops after half a flight of stairs. Which combined risk assessment is correct?
options: RCRI 3 with poor functional capacity below 4 METs, supporting further cardiac assessment
RCRI 4 with poor functional capacity and automatic progression to spinal anesthesia
RCRI 3 with functional capacity at least 4 METs
questions.explanation: Insulin DM, CHF, and Cr >2.0 = 3; TKA is not high-risk surgery. Poor capacity plus RCRI 3 prompts further assessment.

questions.stem: A patient took lisinopril this morning and ate a heavy breakfast at 0700 for a noon elective case. Which issue changes timing, and which primarily changes anesthetic planning?
options: The heavy meal delays the case; lisinopril increases induction-hypotension risk
Lisinopril delays the case; the meal can be addressed with Bicitra
Neither matters if the patient feels well
questions.explanation: A heavy meal needs 8 hours or more, so noon is too early. Taking an ACEI is not itself a cancellation reason but predicts post-induction hypotension.

questions.stem: A cocaine-intoxicated patient has chest pain, BP 200/115, and HR 130. Benzodiazepine treatment does not adequately reduce severe hypertension. Which next agent best treats coronary ischemia and hypertension without pure beta-blockade?
questions.explanation: Benzodiazepines come first; vasodilators like nitroprusside or nitroglycerin are next. Beta-blockers risk unopposed alpha stimulation and coronary vasospasm.
